_comment: The content type each client guesses from a filename extension, and the
only place that mapping is written down for all four. Every client reads
this file in its own test suite, so a change to one implementation that
the others do not follow turns three languages red rather than shipping a
gateway four different Content-Type headers for the same attachment.
The text types carry a charset. Go's mime package appends one to every
text/* it returns, and it is the better answer anyway: a text attachment
with no declared encoding is one the mail client has to guess at, and a
UTF-8 CSV guessed as latin-1 is mojibake in a spreadsheet.
Every extension here is in Go's builtinTypesLower, so Go answers from its
own table rather than the host's mime database. Adding one that is not
would make the Go client's answer depend on which machine it runs on.
